After the council meeting, Mar'dy spend another hard day at work deep into the night. He made detailed orders and messages for the few Flora warriors and aides under his employ. They detailed how Kureta and the industries should be run in his absence. They were detailed up to ten years. He didn't know how long he would be gone. Or if he would come back.

He let out a deep shakey sigh. It felt like leaving Dire Vents, there was less danger but he had grown a bit fatter, out of touch perhaps, he didn't have a hand, how could he defend himself? With this he retired into an uneasy sleep. The preparations were underway, the Flora warriors seemed excited to be deployed for the first time. They had practiced extra hard with him that day to prove their worth. He was still a little bruised and these injuries brought back horrid memories.

He woke up again on a sandy floor. He was in water again, two Lot'dy gladiators circled him, they must have knocked him down. They were throwing their hands up, the crowd cheered and roared. Mar'dy rolled to the side and scrambled to pick up a spear next to him. The spear stayed on the ground, his hand was gone. That same bloody stump. A costly mistake, he looked up to see only the sharp edge of a spear knock him down again.

He awoke again in a dark temple. Naga surrounded him in metal costumes and hoods. Fires burned, somehow burned under the waters. He was tied down. They hissed and clicked in some ancient tongue. Then tentacles started to come out of the altar he was chained to. They wrapped themselves around his limbs and started to tear him apart.

Again he was in the sky, falling, heading toward a mountain of some type. He looked up, a dozen schryke were above him, holding others, the Deva refugees. He looked back down as he fell. He couldn't do anything, he was heading to what looked like chimney. A red dot below him glowed brighter, he was falling towards a giant crucible filled with molten metal. He awoke in a cold sweat, it was already morning. It was all fear. He needed to cure his fear. Rose was right. He needed to go. AS he stepped out of his home, he saw a crowd gathered in the steps leading to his home. "Had they come to say goodbye?"

"There is something you should know about me" he said, "I am a traitor and a failure"

"So am I" Mar'dy said. "But Tempest offered both of us another chance. It is what we turn our lives into now that matters."

He took back the sword and brought him into his office. "Well there are some options for you now. I can't force you to do anything, I want you to know you are free to do whatever you like. "If you do choose to come with me, I can't guarantee you will live. I'm sure that doesn't concern you much does it?"

"I will go with you, for that is what I promised. Though I know not where, or why. I will go, and I will serve you. I will watch your back, and offer what help I can. "The blood of a traitor" he said.

Mar'dy licked the blade as was customary, then cut his own hand offering the same blade back to Sa'vak.

"Stand, we are equal brother."
Sa'vak stood "so it is done", he said "the promise of two traitors, sworn to each other". He shook Mar'dy's hand, their blood intermingling, "blood brothers, a powerful oath".
